item.title: Amsterdam as a 3D city model from AHN4 lidar - Ivana Pallister
item.summary: The national laser scan of a square kilometre of Amsterdam turned into a clean block model, buildings, canals and trees, and flown over slowly.
item.page_text:
AHN measures the whole country with an aircraft laser, about 35 points on every square metre of this part of Amsterdam. Each point comes with a label: ground, building, water or something else.
Raw, it looks like snow. So I rebuilt it. Building points are grouped into parts that share a roof height, every part gets straight walls along its outline, and trees become one smooth canopy. You lose detail, gables and chimneys become steps, but the city suddenly reads.
The flight starts at the Rijksmuseum, whose two towers still come through as stepped spires, and heads north-east over the canals.
Buildings are stone coloured, lighter as they get taller. Trees are olive, canals dark slate. Everything outside the scanned area fades into the page.
AHN4 laser scan (Rijkswaterstaat, Het Waterschapshuis), CC0, via GeoTiles.nl. Model and rendering are my own scripts.
